def selftest() -> int:
    """Synthetic-artifact assertions; exits nonzero on any failure."""
    import tempfile

    ok = True

    def expect(label, actual, wanted):
        nonlocal ok
        status = "ok" if actual == wanted else "FAIL"
        if actual != wanted:
            ok = False
        print(f"  [{status}] {label}: exit {actual} (want {wanted})")

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        td = Path(td)

        def make_zip(path: Path, a_size: int, extra: "dict[str, int] | None" = None):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as zf:
                zf.writestr("bin/a.bin", b"\0" * a_size)
                zf.writestr("bin/b.bin", b"\0" * (10 * 1024))
                for name, size in (extra or {}).items():
                    zf.writestr(name, b"\0" * size)

        base_zip, cur_zip = td / "base.zip", td / "cur.zip"
        make_zip(base_zip, 100 * 1024)
        make_zip(cur_zip, 100 * 1024)
        base = td / "base.tsv"
        r = check(cur_zip, base, 5.0, init_if_missing=True)
        expect("init-if-missing seeds + passes", r, 0)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 104 * 1024)  # +4%: within budget
        expect("within-budget growth passes", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 0)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 106 * 1024)  # +6%: regression
        expect("over-budget growth fails", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 1)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 100 * 1024, {"bin/new.bin": 6 * 1024 * 1024})
        expect("heavy new line fails", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 1)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 80 * 1024)  # still tracked (> 64 KB), 20% smaller
        expect("tracked-line shrink passes", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0), 0)

        make_zip(cur_zip, 106 * 1024)  # reseed overwrites an EXISTING baseline
        expect("reseed rewrites + passes", check(cur_zip, base, 5.0, reseed=True), 0)
        expect("smaller-than-floor still passes", check(base_zip, base, 5.0), 0)
        bigger = td / "bigger.zip"
        make_zip(bigger, 120 * 1024)  # +13% vs the reseeded floor
        expect("post-reseed regrowth fails", check(bigger, base, 5.0), 1)

        tree = td / "root" / "app"
        (tree / "assets").mkdir(parents=True)
        (tree / "index.html").write_bytes(b"\0" * (200 * 1024))
        (tree / "assets" / "x.bin").write_bytes(b"\0" * (150 * 1024))
        dir_base = td / "dir.tsv"
        expect("dir artifact init", check(tree, dir_base, 5.0, init_if_missing=True), 0)
        (tree / "index.html").write_bytes(b"\0" * (220 * 1024))  # +10%
        expect("dir over-budget fails", check(tree, dir_base, 5.0), 1)

        # Deny-list (gh-1331 review): a re-added evicted row below the
        # NEW-line share (5% of TOTAL) passes the plain gate — only
        # --forbid catches it. Floor: 8 MiB TOTAL -> NEW share ~410 KB;
        # the re-added 100 KB row is tracked (> 64 KB) but sub-share.
        deny_zip, deny_base = td / "deny.zip", td / "deny.tsv"
        make_zip(deny_zip, 100 * 1024, {"bin/big.bin": 8 * 1024 * 1024})
        expect("deny floor seeds", check(deny_zip, deny_base, 5.0, init_if_missing=True), 0)
        make_zip(cur_zip, 100 * 1024,
                 {"bin/big.bin": 8 * 1024 * 1024, "evicted/gone.dat": 100 * 1024})
        expect("re-added sub-NEW-share row passes without --forbid",
               check(cur_zip, deny_base, 5.0), 0)
        expect("re-added row fails with --forbid",
               check(cur_zip, deny_base, 5.0, forbid=["^evicted/"]), 1)
        expect("clean artifact passes with --forbid",
               check(deny_zip, deny_base, 5.0, forbid=["^evicted/"]), 0)
        expect("--forbid blocks reseeding the banned shape",
               check(cur_zip, deny_base, 5.0, reseed=True, forbid=["^evicted/"]), 1)

        # Rev-hash churn (#1431): the engine renderer moves under a new
        # 20+hex rev dir on every 3.47.x patch — pure path substitution,
        # identical bytes. Normalization must diff it as a no-op UPDATE,
        # not N brand-new heavyweight lines; vendored breaches warn; the
        # first-party rule keeps its teeth.
        rev_zip, rev_base = td / "rev.zip", td / "rev.tsv"
        old_rev, new_rev = "a" * 40, "b" * 40

        def make_rev_zip(path: Path, rev: str):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as zf:
                zf.writestr(f"panel/app/canvaskit/{rev}/canvaskit.wasm",
                            b"\0" * (7 * 1024 * 1024))
                zf.writestr(f"panel/app/canvaskit/{rev}/canvaskit.js",
                            b"\0" * (90 * 1024))
                zf.writestr("panel/app/main.dart.js", b"\0" * (1024 * 1024))

        make_rev_zip(rev_zip, old_rev)
        expect("rev baseline seeds", check(rev_zip, rev_base, 5.0, init_if_missing=True), 0)
        make_rev_zip(rev_zip, new_rev)
        expect("rev-dir rename is a no-op UPDATE", check(rev_zip, rev_base, 5.0), 0)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(rev_zip, "a") as zf:
            zf.writestr(f"panel/app/canvaskit/{new_rev}/skwasm_new.wasm",
                        b"\0" * (6 * 1024 * 1024))
        expect("new vendored heavyweight warns (passes)", check(rev_zip, rev_base, 5.0), 0)
        expect("strict mode gates the vendored file",
               check(rev_zip, rev_base, 5.0, strict_vendored=True), 1)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(rev_zip, "a") as zf:
            zf.writestr("panel/app/newbin/heavy.bin", b"\0" * (6 * 1024 * 1024))
        expect("new first-party heavyweight still fails", check(rev_zip, rev_base, 5.0), 1)
        # A pre-fix baseline carrying the literal rev hash migrates on load.
        literal_base = td / "rev_literal.tsv"
        literal_base.write_text(
            f"{7 * 1024 * 1024}\tpanel/app/canvaskit/{old_rev}/canvaskit.wasm\n"
            f"{90 * 1024}\tpanel/app/canvaskit/{old_rev}/canvaskit.js\n"
            f"{1024 * 1024}\tpanel/app/main.dart.js\n"
            f"{7 * 1024 * 1024 + 90 * 1024 + 1024 * 1024}\tTOTAL\n")
        make_rev_zip(rev_zip, new_rev)
        expect("literal-rev baseline migrates on load", check(rev_zip, literal_base, 5.0), 0)

    print("selftest:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_emit = sub.add_parser("emit", help="print the TSV manifest")
    p_emit.add_argument("artifact", type=Path)
    p_emit.add_argument("--min-bytes", type=int, default=MIN_BYTES)

    p_chk = sub.add_parser("check", help="manifest + budget gate")
    p_chk.add_argument("artifact", type=Path)
    p_chk.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path, required=True)
    p_chk.add_argument("--budget-pct", type=float, default=5.0)
    p_chk.add_argument("--init-if-missing", action="store_true")
    p_chk.add_argument("--reseed", action="store_true",
                       help="overwrite an EXISTING baseline from this "
                            "artifact and pass (intentional-growth escape "
                            "hatch; commit the rewritten file)")
    p_chk.add_argument("--manifest-out", type=Path)
    p_chk.add_argument("--forbid", action="append", default=[], metavar="REGEX",
                       help="deny-list: fail if any manifest row path matches "
                            "REGEX (repeatable; enforced on check/init/reseed)")
    p_chk.add_argument("--vendored", action="append", default=[], metavar="REGEX",
                       help="extra vendored-prefix regex: breaches on matching "
                            "rows warn instead of failing (#1431; repeatable, "
                            "extends the built-in canvaskit/ default)")
    p_chk.add_argument("--strict-vendored", action="store_true",
                       help="disable the vendored carve-out — every breach "
                            "fails, engine-renderer churn included")

    sub.add_parser("selftest", help="synthetic end-to-end assertions")

    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.cmd == "emit":
        manifest = build_manifest(args.artifact, args.min_bytes)
        for name in sorted(manifest):
            print(f"{manifest[name]}\t{name}")
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "check":
        return check(args.artifact, args.baseline, args.budget_pct,
                     args.init_if_missing, reseed=args.reseed,
                     manifest_out=args.manifest_out, forbid=args.forbid,
                     vendored=args.vendored,
                     strict_vendored=args.strict_vendored)
    return selftest()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` + `release-provenance`

arguments.command:
cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
rows = []
in_table = False
total = None
for line in open('mac_arm64_job.log', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'):
    line = line.replace('\x1b[36;1m','').replace('\x1b[0m','').replace('\x1b[0m','')
    line = re.sub(r'^Build macOS arm64\tSize manifest \+ budget gate \(mac zip\)\t', '', line)
    line = re.sub(r'^....-..-..T[0-9:.]+Z ?', '', line)
    line = line.rstrip('\n')
    if line.startswith('size manifest:'):
        in_table = True; continue
    if not in_table: continue
    if set(line.strip()) == {'-'} and line.strip():
        continue
    m = re.match(r'^\s*(\d+)\s\s(.+?)\s*$', line)
    if m:
        size, name = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2)
        if name == 'TOTAL':
            total = size; in_table = False; continue
        rows.append((size, name))
        continue
    if line.startswith('improvements:'):
        in_table = False
# sort like python sorted() (codepoint order); TOTAL last
rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[1])
with open('new_manifest.tsv','w') as f:
    for s, n in rows:
        f.write(f"{s}\t{n}\n")
    f.write(f"{total}\tTOTAL\n")
print("rows:", len(rows), "TOTAL:", total)
tracked = sum(s for s,_ in rows)
print("tracked sum:", tracked, "filler:", total - tracked)
# sanity: names unique, all >= 64KiB
names = [n for _,n in rows]
assert len(names) == len(set(names)), "dup names"
assert all(s >= 64*1024 for s,_ in rows), "sub-floor row"
import unicodedata
assert all(ord(c) < 128 for n in names for c in n), "non-ascii name"
print("OK")
EOF

arguments.content:
# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2088 [daily-publish] cli leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily-publish `cli` leg red at "Build macOS arm64 — Size manifest + budget gate (mac zip)": the committed macOS arm64 size floor rejects the shipped v1.0.702 app shape because `Fa.app/Contents/Resources/Assets.car` grew +101.6% (93640 → 188792 bytes), far beyond the gate's +5.0% per-line budget.

**Root cause**: `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv` line 26 pins `Assets.car` at 93640 bytes — seeded from the v1.0.634 build (gh-1820). PR #2063 ("Fa 2: messenger redesign and Porcelain app marketing", commit `64712f24`, merged Nov 8) replaced **all seven** `flutter_app/macos/Runner/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/*.png` icons with the new Squircle-V2 brand-mark artwork; every icon PNG grew ~2.2–2.4× (e.g. `app_icon_1024.png` 31619 → 72758 bytes, `app_icon_512.png` 14029 → 37728). Xcode's `actool` compiles the icon set into `Assets.car`, so the compiled catalog roughly doubled. This is **intentional brand growth**, not a regression: nothing in the build pipeline or app code changed shape unexpectedly.

Note on the ticket's auto-extracted "error signature": the quoted `::error::mac arch 'arm64' has no size baseline mapping` line is the *echoed script text* of the `*)` branch of the arch `case` whitelist in `build-macos.yml` (line ~952) — that branch is **not taken** for `arm64` (`arm64|x64) ;;` matches first). The real failure is the second `##[error]` in the log: `size budget regression in fa-macos-arm64-1.0.702-mac.zip (1 line(s) beyond +5.0%): GREW +101.6% Assets.car`. The arch whitelist is fine.

**Impact**: The cli leg's mac zip gate fails → the whole daily-publish run goes red, blocking the daily auto-publish (DMG/notarization, release attachment) until the floor acknowledges the new shape. The gate is working as designed: it caught a real shape change and demands a conscious ack. Only ONE line is beyond budget (`Assets.car`); the rest of the run's shape shift is actually a large contraction — TOTAL fell 116386369 → 74701116 bytes (116.4 MB → 74.7 MB) because `GemmaModelConstraintProvider` (9.4 MB), `LiteRtLm` (26.2 MB), `LiteRtMetalAccelerator` (11.5 MB) and `StreamProxy` frameworks left the bundle, partially offset by the #2063 Fa2 typography presets adding the Geist / IBM Plex / Manrope / PlusJakartaSans / SpaceGrotesk font families plus a liquid-glass shader to flutter_assets (all new lines below the 5%-of-TOTAL NEW-line share, so the gate accepted them).

**Fix approach**: Apply the gate's own documented intentional-growth escape hatch — reseed the floor from the failing run's artifact shape and commit it (`build-macos.yml` step output: "intentional growth? re-seed the floor with: `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check <artifact> --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv --reseed`"). Precedent: gh-1820 (`afdec9f6`, arm64 floor 1.0.634), gh-1954 (`5831b40c`, fa-ios floor), gh-2030 (`9abc95e6`, fa-extension floor). The arm64 zip was not uploaded (the leg failed at the gate), so the authoritative artifact evidence is the manifest table the gate itself printed into run 42761496337's log (56 rows ≥ 64 KiB + TOTAL = the exact `--reseed` output shape). The reseed was performed with the real tool against a fixture of that shape, so the committed TSV is byte-identical to what `--reseed` seeds. Per the same precedent, the floor-pinning test travels with the floor: `test/ci_1820_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart` (pins the v1.0.634 shape byte-exactly) is superseded by `test/ci_2088_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart`, which pins the v1.0.702 shape two ways — the real gate must accept the committed floor against the run's shape, and a `--reseed` round-trip must reproduce the committed file byte-for-byte.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first filing of this ticket.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The daily-publish cli leg red at the mac zip size budget gate: `Fa.app/Contents/Resources/Assets.car` grew +101.6% (93640 → 188792) against the +5% per-line floor in `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv`. PR #2063 replaced all seven macOS `AppIcon.appiconset` PNGs with the heavier Squircle-V2 brand-mark artwork, and `actool` compiles the icon set into `Assets.car` — intentional brand growth, not a regression. (The ticket's quoted "no size baseline mapping" signature is just the echoed script text of the non-taken `case` branch; the real `##[error]` is the size regression.) The same run's shape otherwise contracted: TOTAL 116.4 MB → 74.7 MB as the Gemma/LiteRT on-device frameworks left the bundle, while the #2063 Fa2 typography added several font families.

### Fix

- `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv`: reseeded from the failing run's gate-printed manifest (run 42761496337) with the gate's own documented escape hatch (`check --baseline … --reseed`) — 56 tracked rows + TOTAL 74701116, byte-exact `--reseed` output (gh-1820/gh-1954/gh-2030 precedent).
- `test/ci_2088_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart`: new floor pin (runs the real `scripts/size_manifest.py check` gate against a fixture of the v1.0.702 shape + asserts the committed floor is the byte-exact `--reseed` output).
- `test/ci_1820_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart`: removed — it pins the superseded v1.0.634 shape byte-exactly and reds once the floor moves (the pin travels with the floor).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: `ci_2088` floor test against the stale baseline reproduced the exact CI failure — `GREW + 101.6% Fa.app/Contents/Resources/Assets.car 93640 -> 188792 (1 line(s) beyond +5.0%)`, exit 1.
- After reseed: `dart test test/ci_2088_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart` — 2/2 PASS; `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py selftest` — PASS; extension floor/gate neighbors (ci_1684, ci_2030, gh1847) — 33 PASS.
- Full root suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: <result>

### Notes

- Data-only fix: no product code, no workflow change. The gate keeps its teeth — any future line regrowing >+5% vs the new floor (or a removed framework returning >5% of TOTAL) still fails.
- The x86_64 sibling job self-seeds `fa-macos-x64.tsv` in its workspace each run (no committed floor), so it stayed green; only the arm64 floor needed the reseed.
- The next daily run is expected green on this gate; the seeded floor is committed so the `Upload seeded size baselines` ratchet has nothing new to arm.

PR #2063 replaced all seven macOS `AppIcon.appiconset` PNGs with the heavier Squircle-V2 brand-mark artwork; `actool` compiles the icon set into `Assets.car` — intentional brand growth. The ticket's quoted "no size baseline mapping" line is just the echoed text of the non-taken `case` branch; the real failure is the size regression. Same run otherwise contracted: TOTAL 116.4 MB → 74.7 MB (Gemma/LiteRT frameworks left the bundle) while #2063 Fa2 typography added several font families.

- `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv` — reseeded from the failing run's gate-printed manifest (run 42761496337) with the gate's own escape hatch (`check --baseline … --reseed`); 56 tracked rows + TOTAL 74701116, byte-exact `--reseed` output (gh-1820/gh-1954/gh-2030 precedent).

- `test/ci_1820_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart` — removed: pinned the superseded v1.0.634 shape byte-exactly; the pin travels with the floor.

- RED first: the new test vs the stale floor reproduced the exact CI failure (`GREW + 101.6% … Assets.car 93640 -> 188792`, exit 1).

- Data-only fix (no product/workflow code); the gate keeps its teeth — any future line >+5% vs the new floor still fails.

### Root Cause

The cli leg red at the mac zip size budget gate: `Fa.app/Contents/Resources/Assets.car` grew +101.6% (93640 → 188792) vs the +5% floor in `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv`. PR #2063 replaced all seven macOS `AppIcon.appiconset` PNGs with the heavier Squircle-V2 brand-mark artwork; `actool` compiles the icon set into `Assets.car` — intentional brand growth. The ticket's quoted "no size baseline mapping" line is just the echoed text of the non-taken `case` branch; the real failure is the size regression. Same run otherwise contracted: TOTAL 116.4 MB → 74.7 MB (Gemma/LiteRT frameworks left the bundle) while #2063 Fa2 typography added several font families.

### Fix

- `scripts/size_budget/fa-macos-arm64.tsv` — reseeded from the failing run's gate-printed manifest (run 42761496337) with the gate's own escape hatch (`check --baseline … --reseed`); 56 tracked rows + TOTAL 74701116, byte-exact `--reseed` output (gh-1820/gh-1954/gh-2030 precedent).
- `test/ci_2088_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart` — new floor pin: real `size_manifest.py check` gate must accept the committed floor vs the v1.0.702 shape + `--reseed` round-trip must be byte-identical.
- `test/ci_1820_macos_arm64_size_floor_test.dart` — removed: pinned the superseded v1.0.634 shape byte-exactly; the pin travels with the floor.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: the new test vs the stale floor reproduced the exact CI failure (`GREW + 101.6% … Assets.car 93640 -> 188792`, exit 1).
- Post-fix: `ci_2088` 2/2 PASS; `size_manifest.py selftest` + `scripts/test_size_manifest.py` PASS; ci_1684/ci_2030/gh1847 neighbors 33 PASS; full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: <SUITE_RESULT>.

### Notes

- Data-only fix (no product/workflow code); the gate keeps its teeth — any future line >+5% vs the new floor still fails.
- x86_64 self-seeds `fa-macos-x64.tsv` in-workspace each run (no committed floor), so only the arm64 floor needed this reseed.

**Root cause:** PR #2063 ("Fa 2 / Porcelain app marketing", commit `64712f24`) replaced all seven macOS `AppIcon.appiconset` PNGs with the heavier Squircle-V2 brand-mark artwork (each ~2.2–2.4× bigger); `actool` compiles the icon set into `Assets.car`. Intentional brand growth hitting a stale v1.0.634-seeded floor.
